read.sections.0.text.note: Real people in their usual Thai school spellings: ปี้เซิง (Bi Sheng) and โยฮันเนส กูเทนเบิร์ก (Johannes Gutenberg). "In the 1400s" is ในช่วงปี 1400 ถึง 1499, as KEY_TERMS asks (check). "wheels to shape clay pots" is วงล้อหมุนเพื่อปั้นหม้อ (a potter's wheel).
read.sections.0.text.source: An invention is a new tool, machine or way of doing something. About 5,500 years ago, people in Mesopotamia used wheels to shape clay pots. Later, people put wheels on carts to carry heavy loads of grain and goods, which made farming and trade easier. Printing is another example. About 1,000 years ago in China, a man named Bi Sheng made small clay blocks, each with one written sign. Printers could move the blocks around to print new pages. Later, printers in Korea used metal blocks. In the 1400s, Johannes Gutenberg built a printing press in Germany. Books became cheaper, so more people could read and share ideas.
read.sections.0.text.back: An invention is a new tool, machine or way of doing things. About 5,500 years ago, people in Mesopotamia used a spinning wheel to shape clay pots. Later people attached wheels to carts to carry grain and heavy goods, making farming and trade easier. Printing is another example. About 1,000 years ago in China, a man named Bi Sheng made small clay type pieces, each with one character. Printers could rearrange the type to print new pages. Later printers in Korea used metal type. In the 1400s Johannes Gutenberg built a printing press in Germany. Books became cheaper, so more people could read books and share ideas.

read.sections.0.simpler.source: An invention is a new tool or way to do something. Long ago, people in what is now Iraq used wheels to make pots. Later, people put wheels on carts to carry heavy loads. Printing is another invention. In China, Bi Sheng made small clay blocks, each with one sign. Later, people in Korea made metal blocks. Then Gutenberg made a printing press in Germany. Books cost less, so more people could read.
read.sections.0.simpler.back: An invention is a new tool or way of doing things. Long ago, people in the land that is now Iraq used a wheel to make pots. Later, people attached wheels to carts to carry heavy things. Printing is an invention too. In China, Bi Sheng made small clay type pieces, each with one character. Later, people in Korea made metal type. Then Gutenberg built a printing press in Germany. Books got cheaper, so more people got to read books.
read.sections.0.simpler.note: Second pass: the last sentence said คนจึงได้อ่านมากขึ้น (people read more); changed to คนจำนวนมากขึ้นจึงได้อ่านหนังสือ (more people could read), as the English says.

read.sections.1.text.note: "kerosene lamps" is ตะเกียงน้ำมันก๊าด; the simpler text says ตะเกียงแบบเก่าใช้น้ำมัน. "even without a bank" is แม้ไม่มีบัญชีธนาคาร (a bank account), which is what the English means.
read.sections.1.text.source: Some newer inventions spread very quickly. Mobile phones let people call, send messages and find information. In Kenya, a service that started in 2007 lets people send small amounts of money by phone, even without a bank. Solar lamps are another example. During the day, sunlight charges a battery inside the lamp. At night, the lamp gives light without any power lines. Many families once used lamps that burned kerosene, which made smoke and had to be bought again and again. With a solar lamp, people can cook, read or study after dark. But an invention only helps people who have access to it.
read.sections.1.text.back: Some new inventions spread very fast. Mobile phones let people call each other, send messages and find information. In Kenya, a service that started in 2007 let people send small amounts of money by phone, even without a bank account. Solar lamps are another example. In the daytime, sunlight charges the lamp's battery. At night the lamp gives light without power lines. Many families used to use kerosene lamps, which are smoky and need new fuel again and again. With solar lamps, people can cook, read or study after dark. But an invention only helps people who can access it.

read.sections.1.simpler.source: Some new inventions spread fast. With a mobile phone, people can call, send messages and find news. In Kenya, people can send money by phone. A solar lamp charges in the sun and gives light at night. Old lamps burned oil and made smoke. With a solar lamp, people can read after dark. But an invention only helps if people have access to it.
read.sections.1.simpler.back: Some new inventions spread fast. With mobile phones, people call each other, send messages and get news. In Kenya, people can send money by phone. A solar lamp charges with sunlight, then gives light at night. Old lamps use oil and are smoky. With solar lamps, people can read after dark. But an invention only helps if people can access it.

read.sections.2.text.source: Look at the bicycle trial in Riverstone. Cycling to the market takes 12 minutes instead of 30, so it saves Amara 18 minutes. That is a real benefit. But a bicycle costs 80 tokens, which Hana cannot pay, and repairs need parts and skills. The steps on the direct route are a barrier, because riders must carry their bicycles up them. Some people cannot ride a bicycle, or do not want to. Inventions can also cause problems that no one planned. Cars made travel faster, but they also made the air dirty. So when you study an invention, ask who can use it, who decides and what would help more people.
read.sections.2.text.back: Look at the Riverstone bicycle trial. Cycling to the market takes 12 minutes instead of 30, so it saves Amara 18 minutes. That is a real benefit. But a bicycle costs 80 coins, which Hana can't afford, and repairs need parts and skills. The steps on the direct route are a barrier, because riders must carry their bicycles up them. Some people can't ride or don't want to. Inventions can also cause problems nobody planned. Cars made travel faster but also made the air dirty. So when you study an invention, ask who can use it, who decides, and what would help more people.

read.sections.2.simpler.note: "the direct route" is ทางลัด (a shortcut) in the simpler text, เส้นทางตรง in the standard text.
read.sections.2.simpler.source: Look at the bike trial in Riverstone. By bike, the trip takes 12 minutes, not 30. So Amara saves 18 minutes. That is a benefit. But a bike costs 80 tokens, and Hana cannot pay that. On the short route, riders must carry bikes up steps. That is a barrier. Some people cannot ride a bike. Inventions can also bring problems no one planned. Cars are fast, but they make the air dirty. So ask: Who can use it? Who does it help?

write.example.source: The trial shows that cycling saves Amara 18 minutes on the direct route to the market. One benefit is that she has more time for other work. However, one barrier is the cost. A bicycle costs 80 tokens, so Hana cannot get one. The steps on the direct route are also a barrier. Before giving out more bicycles, I would test the longer route with no steps. I would also ask if people could share bicycles. This would help more people because more of them could use one safely.
write.example.back: The trial shows that cycling saves Amara 18 minutes on the direct route to the market. One benefit is that she has more time for other work. But one barrier is cost. A bicycle costs 80 coins, so Hana can't buy one. The steps on the direct route are a barrier too. Before giving out more bicycles, I would test the longer route with no steps. I would also ask whether people could share bicycles. This would help more people because more people could use bicycles safely.

watch.summary.note: Sensitive: slavery. "cotton gin" is เครื่องแยกเมล็ดฝ้าย; "enslaved people" is ผู้คนที่ถูกทำให้เป็นทาส, as in Lesson 8; "slavery" is ระบบทาส. Keep it short and factual.
watch.summary.source: This video tells the story of the cotton gin, a machine invented in the United States in 1793. Cotton plants grow soft white fibre, which is used to make cloth. Before the machine, workers had to pull the seeds out of the cotton by hand, and this was very slow. The cotton gin did the job much faster. One worker could now do the work of about 10. Growing cotton began to earn much more money, and the cotton business grew fast. But the machine also had a terrible effect that no one planned. Cotton farms grew, and farm owners forced many more enslaved people to work on them. Slavery lasted longer. The video shows that one invention can bring both wealth and great harm.
watch.summary.back: The video tells the story of the cotton gin, a machine invented in the United States in 1793. Cotton plants give soft white fibre used to make cloth. Before this machine, workers had to pick the seeds out of cotton by hand, which was very slow. The cotton gin did this work much faster. Now one worker could do the work of about 10 people. Growing cotton started to make much more money, and the cotton business grew fast. But the machine also had serious results nobody planned. Cotton plantations grew larger, and owners forced even more enslaved people to work on them. So slavery lasted longer. The video shows that one invention can bring both wealth and serious harm.
